fulltext_batch_2026_09_25.changed_understanding: Macklin threshold differs by load component/peak-vs-mean; Ryan net yaw has no steady-relative overshoot despite side/lift peaks, resolving abstract overgeneralization; 1996 and 1998 yaw outcomes differ under different apparatus/metric definitions. Macklin 1997 shear comparison is turbulence-confounded and no reference speed universally collapses coefficients. Ryan 2000 uses updated 5m/22deg shutter gust; an unexplained high-pressure pocket and wake advection prevent treating a wake snapshot as instantaneous body force. Mahig 1971 is an assumed lateral-impulse vehicle response model, not an aerodynamic gust waveform study; tyre cubic locally cross-checked. Klein/Hogue 1980 directly cites and partially reuses DOT technical Volume II; loop modes and steady-model outputs must remain separated. Chadwick 2000 shows geometry-specific leeward pressure peaks and filter limitations; five model lengths not sufficient for steady development in all cases. Nakasato 2017 fixed-steer road validation is separate from the active-driver application; three-run driver trends have quantitative mismatch. Volpe 2014 measured ~21deg local yaw despite 30deg tunnel axes; geometry-specific yaw peaks 16/10%, vortex-load correlations not causal proof. Lewington 2017 one-way advantage depends on metric: both approaches predict lane deviation within one measured SD; comparator uses tuned wind scale and input validation is partial. Okumura 1997 CFD peak and spoiler evidence are conditional; passing comparison uses mismatched bus geometry, and reported resultant wind angle needs arithmetic audit.
